questions.q: Aniline is converted into benzenediazonium chloride by:
options: Conc. HNO₃ and conc. H₂SO₄ at 323 K
questions.explain: Nitrous acid made in situ from sodium nitrite and HCl diazotises the amine, and the salt is stable only in the cold. Nitrate or nitrating mixture does not give the diazonium salt.

questions.q: An aqueous solution of benzenediazonium chloride is allowed to warm above about 283 K. The main organic product is:
questions.explain: Warm water hydrolyses the aryl diazonium ion with loss of N₂, giving phenol; this is why diazotisation is run in ice and the salt is used at once.

questions.q: Which amine gives a yellow, water-insoluble oil with nitrous acid?
questions.explain: A secondary amine is N-nitrosated to (CH₃)₂N–N=O, an N-nitrosamine. Primary amines give diazonium ions (or alcohols with N₂), and tertiary aliphatic amines only form ammonium nitrite salts.

questions.q: Optically pure (R)-butan-2-amine is treated with NaNO₂/HCl in water. The butan-2-ol obtained is best described as:
options: Largely racemised, formed with both retention and inversion
Not formed; only butane and N₂ result
questions.explain: The aliphatic diazonium ion loses N₂ at once to give an open carbocation, which water attacks from either face, so both retention and inversion occur.
